passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756–1791) composed his first pieces at about age five.
• Clara Schumann (1819–1896) gave her first public piano performance at age nine.
• Mozart wrote more than 600 works.
• Schumann became one of the most celebrated pianists in Europe.
stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Mozart and Schumann. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Both showed remarkable talent as children: Mozart composed at about five, and Schumann performed publicly at nine.
Mozart composed his first pieces at about age five and went on to write more than 600 works.
Clara Schumann gave her first public performance at nine and became a celebrated pianist in Europe.
Mozart wrote more than 600 works, while Schumann became one of Europe's most celebrated pianists.
steps: A similarity needs both people and something they share.
Both showed musical talent very young.
Only one choice names both and states the shared trait.
Two choices describe one person only; the last pairs them but shows a difference, not a similarity.
key: For a similarity, look for "both" and a shared feature.
